bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Developed in the mid-1860s from Morse code telegraphic systems, the ticker tape communicated stock prices and order flow on narrow paper tape. Traders like Charles Dow, Jesse Livermore, Richard Wyckoff, and J.P. Morgan built fortunes using only this tape, pencil, and paper.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Originally developed in the mid 1860's as a telegraphic system for communicating using Morse code, the technology was adapted to provide a system for communicating stock prices and order flow.

facts.statement: Richard Wyckoff defined tape reading in Studies in Tape Reading as rapid-fire horse sense—a method for forecasting future market moves from current tape activity by deducing whether large interests are accumulating, distributing, marking up, marking down, or neglecting stocks.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Tape Reading is rapid-fire horse sense. Its object is to determine whether stocks are being accumulated or distributed, marked up or down, or whether they are neglected by the large interests.

facts.statement: Exchange operators manually entered trades onto paper tape using compressed shorthand notations: 'S' separated price quotes, 'SS' designated odd lot trades under 100 shares, 'PR' denoted Preferred stock, and trailing zeroes were often omitted for speed (quoting 10,000 shares as 100).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A short hand code was developed over the years, to try to keep the details as brief as possible, but also communicate all the detailed information required.

facts.statement: While historical paper tickers suffered data delays ranging from a few minutes to several hours, modern electronic tickers display live price and volume ticks instantaneously (such as rising from 45.17 to 45.25 on 99 shares and 45.30 on 10,000 shares) using identical VPA logic.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Well, we have a price that has risen from 45.17 to 45.30 supported by what appears to be strong volume... Today, all the information we see is live.

facts.statement: Figure 1.11 from the Museum of American Finance displays the infamous ticker tape from the morning of October 29, 1929, capturing heavy selling across Goodyear Tyre (GT), United States Steel (X), Radio Corporation (R), and Westinghouse Electric (WX), alongside Jesse Livermore's $100 million short profit.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Fig 1.11 is perhaps the most famous, or infamous example of the ticker tape, from the morning of the 29th October 1929, the start of the Wall Street crash.

facts.statement: Charles Dow, grandfather of technical analysis and co-founder of the Wall Street Journal, never wrote a formal book; following his death in 1902, Sam Nelson and William Hamilton compiled his essays in the 1903 book The ABC of Stock Speculation, coining the term Dow Theory.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Iconic names such as Charles Dow, founder of the Dow Jones, Dow Theory and the Wall Street Journal, and generally referred to as the grandfather of technical analysis.

facts.statement: A core tenet of Charles Dow's methodology is that volume confirms price trends: while a price move on low volume can happen for many unconfirmed reasons (signaling a fake move or trap), price moving in one direction with high or rising volume validates a genuine trend.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: One of Dow's principle beliefs was that volume confirmed trends in price. He maintained that if a price was moving on low volume, then there could be many different reasons. However, when a price move was associated with high or rising volume, then he believed this was a valid move.

facts.statement: Dow classified market trends into three time horizons that have compressed in modern electronic trading: Primary trends lasted 2–3 months (now 2–3 weeks), Secondary pullbacks lasted 2–3 weeks (now 2–3 days), and Minor fluctuations lasted 2–3 days (now 2–3 hours).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Regardless of whether you are scalping as a speculator in stocks, bonds, currencies the techniques you will discover here are as valid today as they were almost 100 years ago.

facts.topic: Three Stages of a Market Trend
facts.statement: Dow defined three distinct stages of a trend: first, the Accumulation Phase where smart money quietly buys wholesale inventory after a decline; second, the Public Participation Phase (the longest technical trend-following stage); and third, the Distribution Phase where insiders sell at retail to FOMO buyers.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: He defined the first stage of a bullish trend as, ‘the accumulation phase’, the starting point for any trend higher. He called the second stage ‘the public participation phase’ which could be considered the technical trend following stage.

facts.statement: Dow advocated analyzing sector indices rather than individual equities to separate risk types: Unsystematic risk affects only an isolated company (such as earnings or analyst ratings), whereas Systematic risk reflects broad macroeconomic forces affecting all stocks within an index simultaneously.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: For this powerful technique we have to thank the great traders of the last century, who laid the foundations of what we call technical analysis today.

facts.statement: Dow pioneered cross-market analysis by creating benchmark indices like the Dow Jones Transportation Index to validate industrial performance; genuine economic growth requires rising industrial output to be matched by transportation activity, whereas divergence between related indices warns of weakness.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The Tape Reader aims to make deductions from each succeeding transaction... gauging the momentary supply and demand in particular stocks and in the whole market, comparing the forces behind each and their relationship, each to the other and to all.

facts.topic: Department Store and Drop of Water Analogies
facts.statement: Wyckoff compared a tape reader to a department store manager adjusting wholesale orders and markdowns based on shelf turnover, and noted that 'the same elements will be found in a drop of water as in the ocean,' proving VPA works identically from 1-minute to monthly charts.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: method for forecasting from what appears on the tape now, what is likely to happen in the future... gauging the momentary supply and demand in particular stocks and in the whole market.

facts.topic: Gunpowder and Nothing New Under the Sun
facts.statement: Opening with Ecclesiastes 1:9 ('Nihil sub sole'—nothing new under the sun) and Livermore's rule of unchanging human psychology, Coulling states that price and volume are weak in isolation, but combined they form an explosive gunpowder combination that forecasts market moves.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: If you thought that Volume Price Analysis was a new concept. Think again. This was the approach used by the iconic traders of the past... and how little the concepts have changed in over a 100 years.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
